items.title: Jets place Dylan DeMelo on injured reserve
items.desc: DeMelo sustained what appeared to be a leg injury during the Jets’ game against the Stars on Thursday.

stories.take:
Per Daily Faceoff, the Jets have placed defenseman Dylan DeMelo on injured reserve after what appeared to be a leg injury in Thursday's game against the Stars.

DeMelo's results have run a little ahead of his play so far this season. He has one goal and seven assists in 20 games, and the 0.19 goals he has scored above what his chances would predict is small. The bigger concern is that Winnipeg has controlled less of the chance quality when he's on the ice at five-on-five, with a 45.62 percent share of expected goals (the quality of shots taken versus allowed). That is below the team's 48 percent at even strength, and the Jets are 2.95 percentage points better without him. So the injury hurts depth and penalty killing, where he's used, more than it removes a driver of play. That matters for a Winnipeg team sitting at 9-8-3 with a penalty kill allowing 0.85 expected goals a game, well behind Dallas at 0.58.

Going by how the coach has used his players, Haydn Fleury, at 12:56 a night, is next in line for DeMelo's minutes. We'd expect a step down in trust on those penalty kills.

items.title: Blue Jackets’ Sean Monahan leaves game with upper-body injury
items.desc: Monahan has one goal and six assists for seven points in 17 games with Columbus in 2026-27.

stories.take: Daily Faceoff reports Sean Monahan left Columbus's game with an upper-body injury, and it lands on a player whose season hasn't found its footing. Monahan has one goal on 3.55 expected goals (the quality of his chances) through 17 games, 2.55 below what those chances usually return, and seven points while playing about 16 minutes a night. Last season he had 36 points in 78 games. The Blue Jackets are 7-10-0 and have had 46% of the expected goals, so they have little cushion for losing a center who also sits on the power play (three power-play points). His five-on-five numbers have been soft (43% of expected goals with him on the ice), but a thin lineup feels any absence. No timeline has been reported.

items.title: Avalanche’s MacKinnon, Makar exit game with lower-body injuries
items.desc: Off to an 11-6-2 start, the Avalanche could see both of their all-world stars miss time.

stories.take: Daily Faceoff reports that Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar both left Colorado's game on Thursday with lower-body injuries, and no timeline has been given for either. For a team built around two players like these, that's the whole story until there's an update. The Avalanche are 11-6-3 and have taken 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), one of the better process numbers around. They've also scored 12.8 more goals than their chances usually return, a finishing edge that runs through their stars. Denver Gazette's Evan Rawal was already writing last week about how poorly Colorado's power play compares with others; that unit would feel this most.

items.title: Wild’s Joel Eriksson Ek leaves game with injury
items.desc: Eriksson Ek has six goals and 11 assists for 17 points in 20 games with the Wild in 2026-27.

stories.take: Daily Faceoff reports Joel Eriksson Ek left Minnesota's game with an injury, and he's one of the most important pieces on one of the league's best teams. The Wild are 14-3-4 with 56% of the expected goals (the quality of chances). With Eriksson Ek on the ice at five on five they've had 59%, about nine points better than when he sits. He has 17 points and seven on the power play, and his chances have been even better than his scoring: 11.25 expected goals on his own shots against six goals. His 1.66 expected goals per 60 is well above last season's 1.16. Minnesota has had strong goaltending (14.4 goals fewer allowed than its chances against deserved), which helps absorb a loss, but not one like this. No timeline yet.

items.title: Penguins could be significant sellers at Trade Deadline
items.desc: The Penguins’ Kyle Dubas has plenty of impactful veterans he could sell at the trade deadline for future assets.

stories.take: Daily Faceoff makes the case that Kyle Dubas and the Penguins could be significant sellers at the trade deadline, with plenty of veterans to move for future assets. The standings back up the conversation: Pittsburgh is 7-10-2 with 16 points. Our numbers make it a little less clear-cut. The Penguins have had 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), close to even, and they've scored 4.7 fewer goals than those chances usually return, while their goaltending has been almost exactly average. That's the profile of a middling team that has been a bit unlucky, not a bad one. It doesn't argue against selling, especially with an older core, but it does mean the record may flatter the case for a teardown a little.

stories.take: Patrick Kane is off injured reserve and expected back against Buffalo, Daily Faceoff reports, after missing the last few games with an upper-body injury. Chicago needs whatever he brings: the Blackhawks are 5-13-1, have been outscored 78-42 and have had only 42% of the expected goals (the quality of chances). Kane's own line is quiet, one goal and nine points in 16 games, with his shooting 2.8 goals below his chances. The bigger story is what's happened around him. At five on five, Chicago has had just 37% of the expected goals with Kane on the ice. Last season in Detroit he scored 57 points in 67 games. One return doesn't fix a team allowing 3.58 expected goals per 60.

stories.take: The Sabres activated Alex Lyon from injured reserve and moved Konsta Helenius there, Daily Faceoff reports. Lyon had been out since a shoulder injury in a September preseason game, and his return is the part that matters for the standings. Buffalo is 8-7-4 with a dead-even chance share (49.8% of the expected goals), yet it has allowed 5.07 more goals than the chances against it deserved. That gap is mostly goaltending, and it's the kind a healthy extra goalie can help close. Helenius has three points in 11 games at about 13 minutes a night; the Sabres have broken even at five on five with him out there (51% of expected goals), so his absence costs depth more than offence.

stories.take: The Islanders get two players back and lose one, Daily Faceoff reports: Jean-Gabriel Pageau is out with a lower-body injury, while Ryan Pulock and Matias Maccelli return to the lineup. Pageau has a goal and seven assists in 17 games. The returns matter more than the box score suggests, because New York's record has been carried by its net. The Islanders are 8-6-4 but have had only 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and they've allowed 12.2 fewer goals than the chances against them deserved. A defenceman like Pulock is the kind of help that could ease that dependence. Losing Pageau, a long-time defensive center, cuts the other way.

stories.take: Daily Faceoff reports Kevin Fiala makes his season debut against the Islanders, his first game since the leg injury he suffered playing for Switzerland at the Winter Olympics in February. For the Kings, he can't come soon enough. Los Angeles is 5-9-2, but the hockey has been better than the record: the Kings have 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and they've scored about 5.5 fewer goals than those chances deserved. Fiala is a finisher on a team that has been short of finishing, so his return addresses the right problem. The other problem is in net, where the Kings have allowed about 6.4 more goals than expected. The Islanders are a decent place to restart: they give up 3.53 expected goals per 60, and their record (7-6-4) leans on goaltending that has saved about 11 goals more than expected.

items.title: Nikita Kucherov is red-hot since trade request
items.desc: Kucherov has racked up 11 points in the six games since it came out that he wouldn’t re-sign with Tampa.

stories.take: The Athletic asks whether Tampa Bay should make one more run or trade Nikita Kucherov and reset, arguing that letting him walk could effectively close the Lightning's window. Meanwhile, Daily Faceoff points out that he has 11 points in the six games since word got out that he won't re-sign. A player who has asked out is supposed to be a distraction. Kucherov is playing like a reminder of what Tampa would be giving up: 26 points in 18 games, after 130 last season. The team around him is 12-4-2 with 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), so this isn't a seller looking for an exit. Our one caution on the hot run: his on-ice results are running about 6.4 goals ahead of the chances, so some of the recent points are bounces. The talent isn't. That's what makes the decision hard: the Lightning look like a contender, with their best player headed for the door.

items.title: Blackhawks GM Kyle Davidson stands by Jeff Blashill, says he's actively seeking trades
items.desc: Kyle Davidson expressed support for coach Jeff Blashill amid a six-game losing streak. “I believe in Blash and his group,” Davidson said. “The players do, too. We’re aligned in that.”

stories.take: Kyle Davidson isn't blinking. The Athletic reports the Blackhawks GM is standing by coach Jeff Blashill through a six-game losing streak and says he is actively looking for trades. The record is 4-13-1, nine points from 18 games, and our numbers say this isn't simply bad luck: Chicago has only 42% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and allows 3.67 expected goals an hour. The goaltending has made it worse, letting in about 9.6 more goals than the shots deserved. That last part is the piece a coach can't fix and a trade might. Backing Blashill makes sense if Davidson believes the process will improve with better players; the numbers suggest the roster needs them, and the market for help is where he says he's looking.

A 5-10-6 team that is losing the chance battle is a difficult place to be a young star, whatever the paperwork says.

items.desc: After months of speculation, a trade request, and a standoff between the Winnipeg Jets and Connor Hellebuyck, the 33-year-old attempted to clear the air on Tuesday in his return to the city he called home for the past 11 seasons.

stories.take:
Scott Arniel isn't pretending the Connor Hellebuyck trade was amicable. Asked by The Hockey News about New Jersey sitting Hellebuyck ahead of his return to Canada Life Centre, the Jets coach's answer made the headline: "He just gave up on us."

That is the story, and it will follow Hellebuyck into Winnipeg whenever he does play there. On the ice, the split so far is less dramatic than the words. In five games for the Devils he's at +1.46 goals saved above expected (saves beyond what the shot quality predicts), good but not carrying anyone, on a 13-5-0 team that takes 59% of the expected goals. Winnipeg is 7-8-3, has 48% of the chances and has scored 7.2 fewer goals than its looks usually produce. The Jets' hole is at the other end of the rink, which probably makes hearing about the goalie harder, not easier.
